lines.speaker: A
lines.text: A financial headline lands, and a few seconds later somebody wants to know what it means for a stock. AINewsTracker is a Python service built around that moment, from collecting the news to testing strategies against it.

lines.speaker: B
lines.text: So it's a news reader that thinks a little?

lines.speaker: A
lines.text: Sort of. It's a web application from AlgoÉTS, built with FastAPI. It collects financial news, analyses the text of each article and exposes what it finds through an API.

lines.speaker: B
lines.text: Where does the news come from?

lines.speaker: A
lines.text: From RSS feeds, from GNews and from other feeds you configure. There's also a seeding step that loads company data and news from outside sources, so the service has material to work with.

lines.speaker: B
lines.text: And what does analysing the text actually give you?

lines.speaker: A
lines.text: Sentiment, topics, and an allocation of tickers, so you know which companies an article is about. Articles end up in MongoDB, and Redis handles caching.

lines.speaker: A
lines.text: Quite cleanly. One main file assembles the service and registers the route groups: news, articles, companies, users, seeding and strategies. News goes through a processing service, then text metrics, then a repository layer before it reaches the database.

lines.speaker: B
lines.text: You said strategies. Where do those fit?

lines.speaker: A
lines.text: That's the second half of the story. A separate path takes the stored information and runs historical backtests. You can ask for a strategy to run for a single company, or for a whole list of them.

lines.speaker: B
lines.text: So the news side and the trading side share the same data.

lines.speaker: A
lines.text: Exactly. You can create and read articles, look a company up by its ticker, even read an article's score. And it runs either through Poetry or with Docker Compose, with FastAPI generating a documentation page for every route.

lines.speaker: B
lines.text: Is there more to see in the written version?

lines.speaker: A
lines.text: Yes. The full page has the architecture diagram, and a companion article follows one piece of news from an incoming feed all the way to a stored article. Worth a read if you like seeing the plumbing.
